category_title: Students who exhibit frustration-based crying and self-abusive behavior during long tasks
student_description: Shaun is an 11-year-old student who becomes easily overwhelmed and exhibits severe distress (crying, whining, self-abusive behavior) when faced with long tasks or physical distance from teachers. He uniquely requires tasks to be strictly segmented into single units and needs staff to maintain very close physical proximity to stay engaged and regulated.

criteria.rationale: Presenting all work at once (such as a stapled packet) triggers severe frustration and self-abusive behavior in Shaun.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must present only one worksheet or single step of the task at a time, explicitly avoiding giving him a large packet or the entire assignment at once.

criteria.rationale: Shaun requires close physical proximity (within 0.3m) to maintain engagement and prevent off-task or distressed behaviors.
criteria.check: The tutor must explicitly establish or maintain close physical proximity (e.g., sitting right next to him, within 0.3 meters) while giving instructions, rather than stepping back or directing him from a distance.
